facts_of_case: The wife challenged the trial court's judgment accepting a petition filed under section 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The husband claimed that the wife was still married to her first husband when she married him. The wife denied deserting the husband and alleged that he manhandled her family members.

legal_principles.principle: A custom cannot be extended by analogy nor one custom can be deduced from another.
legal_principles.held: The law on the point is fairly settled. Our own Hon'ble High Court has held in Asha Rani Vs., Gulshan Kumar, AIR 1995 Punjab & Haryana 287 that custom cannot be extended by analogy nor one custom can be deduced from another.
cited_cases: Asha Rani Vs., Gulshan Kumar, (Year) AIR 1995 Punjab & Haryana 287

legal_principles.principle: A valid marriage can be dissolved by a decree of divorce passed by the court of competent jurisdiction and not in any proceedings before the Panchayat.
legal_principles.held: It is also held by a D.B. Of our own Hon'ble High Court in Rajesh Kumar Madaan Vs. Mrs. Mamta alias Veena, (2005-2) The Punjab Law Reporter 196 that a valid marriage can be dissolved by a decree of divorce passed by the court of competent jurisdiction and not in any proceedings before the Panchayat.
cited_cases: Rajesh Kumar Madaan Vs. Mrs. Mamta alias Veena, (2005-2) The Punjab Law Reporter 196

legal_principles.principle: Any marriage solemnized between two Hindus in contravention of the provisions of section 5(i) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 is null and void.
legal_principles.held: It is also held by a D.B. Of our own Hon'ble High Court in Surjit Singh Vs. Mohinder Pal Singh & Ors. Vol.XI (1987) Marriage Law Journal 206 that any marriage solemnized between two Hindus in contravention of the provisions of section 5(i) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 is null and void.
cited_cases: Surjit Singh Vs. Mohinder Pal Singh & Ors., Vol.XI (1987) Marriage Law Journal 206

legal_principles.principle: A marriage in contravention of clause (i) of Section 5 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 is null and void.
legal_principles.held: Clause (i) of Section 5 lays down, for a lawful marriage, the necessary condition that neither party should have a spouse living at the time of the marriage. A marriage in contravention of this condition, therefore, is null and void.

outcome.final_order: The appeal was allowed, and the trial court's judgment was set aside.
